# PlayFair reference corpus

`reference.json` records results from the original C implementation in MirrPane
commit `06901920ba0183db8648682b6a41c0205dedeea5`, before the pure Go port.
The source is UxPlay's GPLv3 `lib/playfair` implementation. The reference DLL was
built with 64-bit MinGW GCC using `-O2 -fno-strict-aliasing` and `-lm`.

The reproducible corpus uses xorshift32 with initial state `0x6d697272`. Each
generated byte updates state by `state ^= state << 13`, `state ^= state >> 17`,
`state ^= state << 5` (all modulo 2^32), then takes the low byte.

For each of 1,024 cases, generate a 164-byte message and 72-byte EKEY; overwrite
the first five message bytes with `FPLY\x03` and byte 12 with `case % 4`. Compute
`playfair_decrypt(message, ekey)`. Generate a 64-byte block and 16-byte seed, then
compute `sap_hash(block)` and `modified_md5(block, seed)`. Concatenate the three
16-byte outputs into one SHA256 stream in that order. Its digest is stored in
the file, together with the first sixteen individual vectors for debugging.

Tests regenerate the same input stream in Go and compare against the frozen C
results. Normal builds and tests never compile or execute C code.
